finding: Diagnostic found during Phase B2.3: python-flint truncates every arb_series at ctx.cap (default 10), whatever prec= is passed. The B1 generator (b1_cert._taylor, N = 16) and the B1 checker (b1_check.Model.taylor, N = 20) ask for longer series and pad the returned coefficients with zeros, so their near-regime Taylor models silently drop the coefficients from index 10 on, including the remainder. This script measures the effect and re-checks the stored B1 certificate. It reads B1's code and data and modifies neither.
conclusion: The defect is in the B1 code path, not in the stored B1 data: the stored certificate passes B1's own checker with complete series (ctx.cap = 32) as well as with the default cap, and the B2.3 checker re-verifies every imported delta-ball without Taylor series. A corrected generator produces different but equally valid bytes (another semantic hash), so the B1 test that compares fresh and stored semantic hashes would fail after a fix.
proposed_erratum (not applied; B1 is aud: b1_cert._taylor and b1_check.Model.taylor: set ctx.cap to the requested length for the call and assert that no returned series is longer than requested (never pad a truncated series).

Keep the audited certificate data/B1_kappa_certificate.json (semantic 616817fc...8518c6), which the corrected checker accepts; replace the fresh-versus-stored hash test by 'the fresh build passes the corrected checker' and 'the stored certificate passes the corrected checker'.
Add a regression test on the series length; record the erratum in NOTES.md section 5 and the audit folder; a short targeted re-audit of the erratum is a gate decision.
